title: inHabit
team: Andrea Cutroni, Elena Corio, Symon Kipkemei, Marina Osmolovska, Giovanni Carlo Volpe
description: An AI spatial-intelligence copilot that turns a description of daily routines into the housing layout that actually fits them.
body: inHabit bridges architectural layouts and daily routines under the brief "Describe your day. Find your layout." Natural-language text is converted into structured spatial criteria to help households, architects and real-estate agents evaluate housing options.

Built on LangGraph, Anthropic's API and a NetworkX spatial graph, the tool extracts user preferences, runs graph-based semantic search across 800+ synthetic floor plans, and overlays the user's daily routine onto candidate layouts alongside a daylight analysis — scoring fit, simulating daylight and visualizing the routine before a final layout is selected.

sections.title: Approach
body: Three moves, in order: read the brief, search the space of layouts, then score what comes back. Each one is a separate agent step rather than a single prompt, so the reasoning behind a recommendation stays inspectable.

nodes.label: 01. Understand
items: Parse routines and preferences into structured queries

nodes.label: 02. Explore
items: Search layouts through graph reasoning and semantic embeddings

nodes.label: 03. Evaluate
items: Score layout fit, simulate daylight, visualize routines

sections.title: Workflow
body: The pipeline behind those three moves. Synthetic plans are generated and exported, their furniture clustered into a catalogue, each layout encoded as a semantic description plus a spatial graph, and an agent graph reasons over the result — with benchmarking across prompts and LLM providers closing the loop.

sections.title: What It Does
body: A household describes its day in plain language. inHabit turns that into spatial criteria, searches 800+ synthetic plans for the closest fit, and then explains the match — room by room, hour by hour, and against daylight.

scenes.title: 01 — Understand Brief
scenes.caption: The household describes itself in its own words; the copilot parses it into rooms, adjacencies and constraints.

scenes.title: 02 — Search the Layout Space
scenes.caption: Every plan in the dataset embedded as a point. Best matches surface near the query, and any two can be interpolated between.

scenes.title: 03 — Select the Best Option
scenes.caption: The chosen layout with its area breakdown and a fit score across rooms, lifestyle, access, adjacency and size.

scenes.title: 04 — Analyze Daylight
scenes.caption: The same plan re-read as daylight autonomy, room by room, with day and night areas scored separately.

scenes.title: 05 — Visualize Routine
scenes.caption: The household placed in the plan hour by hour — at 21:00, who is where and doing what.

scenes.title: 06 — Evaluate & Explain
scenes.caption: One room interrogated: its area, its character, and the adjacencies that earned or cost it points.

sections.title: MCP Tools
body: Python, Grasshopper and Rhino are wired together through MCP, so custom tools and analyses run inside a single pipeline rather than being exported between applications.

sections.title: Graph-Based Design Exploration
body: Each layout is encoded as a graph of spatial relationships. The search combines semantic descriptions generated through Anthropic’s API with that graph structure, so a query can be about how a home works, not only what it contains.
